narrative.summary: Antigua and Barbuda has no AI-specific law, strategy or guidance. Its only AI-relevant binding instrument is the general Data Protection Act 2013, which governs the personal data used to train and run AI systems. The 2024 and 2025 Throne Speeches say the Ministry of Legal Affairs is drafting AI legislation with CARICOM partners.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Information, Communication Technologies and Utilities
narrative.review_notes: This review was updated on 18 October 2026. The laws portal, the Official Gazette, the government website (Throne Speeches and 2026 Cabinet reports) and the digital transformation portal were searched, and no new AI-specific document was found. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI material from the ICT ministry, the freedom of information office and Parliament. The announced AI legislation and an AI readiness assessment are tracked as leads.

instruments.current_status: Act No. 10 of 2013, assented to 28 October 2013 and published in the Official Gazette Vol. XXXIII No. 64 of 7 November 2013; listed as current law on the official legislation portal (laws.gov.ag) in October 2026 with no amending Act listed. The Act has no commencement section; no separate commencement date is stated in the official text. It contains no provision on automated decision-making or AI. No AI-specific law, bill or strategy had been published as of October 2026 (the 2024 and 2025 Throne Speeches direct the Ministry of Legal Affairs to draft AI legislation; see leads).
instruments.summary: Antigua and Barbuda's general data protection law, covering personal data processed by public bodies and private bodies. It requires consent for processing (with listed exceptions such as contract, legal obligation and vital interests) and sets principles on notice and choice, disclosure, security, retention, data integrity and access, plus data-subject rights of access and rectification and special rules for sensitive personal data. Enforcement is given to the Information Commissioner under the Freedom of Information Act 2004, and offences carry fines of up to XCD 100,000 or five years' imprisonment on indictment; it is the main law governing personal data used to train or run AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only national law that governs the personal data used by AI systems; no AI-specific or automated-decision provisions.

leads.title: Artificial intelligence legislation (being drafted by the Ministry of Legal Affairs)
leads.note: The 2024 Speech from the Throne (7 December 2023, para. 8; https://ab.gov.ag/pdf/throne_speech/2024_throne_speech.pdf) says the Government has assigned the Ministry of Legal Affairs to craft AI legislation with CARICOM Secretariat assistance; the 2025 Speech from the Throne (28 November 2024, para. 41; https://ab.gov.ag/pdf/throne_speech/2025_throne_speech.pdf) directs the Ministry to collaborate with CARICOM counterparts to draft AI laws. No bill on the official bills list (laws.gov.ag/bills) as of 12 October 2026; the 2026 Throne Speeches do not mention AI. Promote when a bill is published. 18 October 2026: still no AI bill on the official bills list or in the Official Gazette search; 2026 Cabinet reports do not mention it.

leads.title: Antigua and Barbuda UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment (RAM) report
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Information, Communication Technologies (with UNESCO and UWI Five Islands)
leads.note: Media report a RAM pilot led by the Ministry of ICT, a validation workshop in September 2024 and a planned launch at the UWI Five Islands AI conference (June 2025). No report found on an official Antigua and Barbuda government site; a UNESCO publication would be regional-body material, not a national record. Check whether the Government adopts or publishes it. 18 October 2026: ICT ministry website still could not be accessed; no report found on the government or digital transformation portals.

leads.title: Digital Transformation Framework / national digitalization roadmap
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Information, Communication Technologies and Utilities (with the UN Development System)
leads.note: The official digital-transformation portal (ab.gov.ag/digitaltransformation) describes a UN-supported Framework to inform a national digitalization strategy (Phase 1: UNDP Digital Readiness Assessment, draft preliminary findings September 2023, no AI content; Phase 2: November 2023 visioning workshop and roadmap). No adopted strategy or roadmap text published; promote only if a published strategy with an AI pillar appears.
